title: the proof of the table reads the state of the place and compares the fan with the runtime
intent: The wave that repairs the proof of the track A (the wave A3): the check of the table of the machine promised a cell and proved a label, and the discriminator of wave 80 found the reason -- the two branches that read the state of a place were dead code, because they took `(cdr (cdr form))' where the arguments of a form are `(cdr form)'.  Every cell was witnessed by any place of the label, and a runtime that took the move of `deciding' from `post-decide' instead passed.  The table of the machine and the code of the runtime are honest; the proof is not.  The wave does not touch the kernel: it makes the check such, what the promise was.  (1) The state of a place is read: the arguments of a form are `(cdr form)', and the guard around the place says which states it admits.  (2) The cell and the state `FROM' are bound to each other: for every cell of the table there is a live place, and the state of that place holds the `FROM' of the cell -- a place that takes the move of the cell from another state is named.  (3) A fan of a label is compared with the runtime and not with the table: the runtime does not narrow the fan, and the fan ends the run in one state.  (4) 'Live for the runtime' and 'live for the tests' are two different things: a root of the graph of the runtime is an autoload cookie or a reference of a top-level form of `lib/'; a definition that only the tests or the scripts call is dead for the runtime, and a move in such a place is not a move of the runtime.  (5) An error of the check is a verdict and not the death of the process: the union and the intersection of a single set do not call `cl-union' and `cl-intersection' with one list, and the whole run stands in a `condition-case'.  (6) The two checks that added no proof are gone, and the table is checked to be well formed instead.  The claim `every-transition-of-the-table-is-taken' keeps its id and is amended, not rewritten (the precedent is §16.28): the promise becomes exactly what the check proves.  A guard that says nothing about the state is a case of its own: such a cell rests on the machine alone, and the check counts those cells and names them -- sixteen of the thirty-one cells rest on such a guard, and the runtime alone can make them strong.
objection: The claim is about a proof and not about a run: the check is static on purpose, because there is no run that takes every move of the table -- a run that meets no busy provider never takes `rate-blocked', and a run that never grows long never takes `budget-overflow'.  The static check answers about the whole kernel at once, and it answers the same way twice.  The price is named: the state of a place is read from the guard around it, and a guard that says nothing about the state excludes no state -- such a place witnesses the cell of its label weakly, and sixteen of the thirty-one cells rest on such a place.  The check counts them and names them, so a reader sees how much of the proof rests on them.  The runtime alone can make them strong, and `lib/yeah-turn.el' is the file of the author of the wave 80.  The liveness of a place is the liveness of the runtime: a definition that only the tests call is dead for the runtime, and the check does not measure the liveness for the tests -- that is a property of its own.  The check never dies: an error of the check is a verdict and not the death of the process, because a check that crashes has not bitten.  The wave touches no code of the kernel, and the table of the machine and the code of the runtime are honest -- the wave repairs the proof, and the proof was the lie.
refuted_by: a cell of the table of the machine is not a move the machine makes, or a label of the table has no live place in the runtime where a run takes that move, or a live place takes the move of a cell from a state the cell does not lead from, or the runtime takes a move the machine does not have, or the runtime narrows a fan of the table, or a fan of the table does not end in one state, or a state of the machine is not reachable from the first one through the cells of the table, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The claim of the wave is amended and not rewritten: the id `every-transition-of-the-table-is-taken' is the same, the text says what the check proves, the `falsifier' names the new failures, and the `control' moved to a mutation of the runtime: the tick of `user-prompt' is moved from the state `idle' to the state `deciding'.  Ten controls were applied to copies of the tree on 2026-11-20 -- seven by the writer of the wave and eight by the parent, and the parent's eight were made independently of the report of the writer.  Every one of them ended with the verdict the control asked for.  (1) The honest tree -- the code 0, and the report says: thirty-one cells, seventeen labels, eleven states, twenty-three places of a tick in the kernel and all of them live.  (2) The tick of `user-prompt' is moved from `idle' to `deciding' -- the check says «the runtime takes the move from another state» for the cell `(idle user-prompt . deciding)' and «the place stands in a state the machine has no move from»; code 1.  (3) The fan of `error' is narrowed in `lib/yeah-turn.el:320' -- the check says «the runtime narrows the fan (deciding)»; code 1.  (4) The tick of `nudge' is taken out of the runtime -- «the runtime does not take the move» for the cell `(post-decide nudge . deciding)'; code 1.  (5) The same tick is put into a definition of `lib/' that only the tests call -- the check still says «the runtime does not take the move», because the place is dead for the runtime; code 1.  (6) The same definition with the cookie of an autoload -- the cookie makes the definition a root of the runtime, and the check answers 0: the liveness is decided by the runtime and not by the tests.  (7) The defect of D6 is put back -- the arguments of the form are read as `(cdr (cdr form)' again -- and the check answers 0, but the proof empties: twenty-nine of the thirty-one cells rest on a guard that says nothing about the state, against sixteen on the honest tree.  The fix is load-bearing and it is measured.  (8) An error inside the check -- «the check could not read the kernel»; code 1.  The measurement of the wave: the check is 793 lines and 35.7 kB, and it goes in 4.1 seconds; the table has thirty-one cells, seventeen labels and eleven states; the kernel has twenty-three places of a tick, and all of them are live for the runtime; sixteen cells are strong and sixteen rest on a guard that says nothing about the state; the fan of `interrupt' is the one fan the runtime does not state the states of, and the check names it.  The full set of the checks of the method and the unit tests are green.
